newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., mayor proposes $445 million budget.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., mayor proposes $445 million budget.

text.p: Tampa, Fla., Mayor Dick Greco has proposed a $445 million budget for fiscal 1998 that leaves property taxes unchanged but raises water and trash collection fees.

The proposal introduced Thursday increases spending by $18 million over last year, with most of the added revenue coming from enterprise and operating tax funds. It contains about $3 million in contingency reserves.

It would add $1 per month to solid waste collection fees and $1.40 per month to the average water bill, an increase of about $30 a year for the average family. Greco said the increases were needed to upgrade an incinerator and offset rising operating and capital costs in the water department.
Property taxes will remain at 6.539 mills.

The budget calls for development of a new police headquaters and two substations, to be funded mainly with the city's share of revenues from the half-cent sales tax increase that Hillsborough County voters approved last fall.
